1. (Currently Amended) A proofed frozen dough comprising: (a) a dough mixture of flour, water, and optionally additives, the dough mixture defining a dough matrix; (b) gas bubbles dispersed throughout the dough matrix, wherein the gas bubbles are produced during proofing and comprise carbon dioxide; (c) a spent yeast component comprising yeast that has been substantially depleted of fermentative activity during proofing; and (d) a preserved yeast component comprising yeast that remains viable and capable of fermentation after freezing and during subsequent baking.

2. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough comprises about 1 to about 8 wt.% of the spent yeast component.

3. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the spent yeast component comprises yeast from cream yeast, compressed yeast, semi-dry yeast, frozen yeast, active dry yeast, instant yeast, or a combination thereof.

4. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 3, wherein the yeast has been spent during proofing.

5. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the spent yeast component has a yeast vitality of less than 25% of its initial vitality, and wherein the spent yeast component contributes to gas production during the proofing stage prior to freezing.

6. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the preserved yeast component has a yeast vitality of at least 50% of its initial vitality, and wherein the preserved yeast component is capable of producing additional gas during baking after the frozen dough is thawed and heated.

7. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough comprises about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the preserved yeast component.

8. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the preserved yeast component comprises encapsulated yeast, fat-coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof, wherein the encapsulation or coating protects the yeast from freezing stress and preserves yeast viability during frozen storage.

9. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough has a volume, and wherein the gas bubbles make up about 30 to about 90% of the volume of the frozen dough, wherein the gas bubbles are produced by the spent yeast component during proofing prior to freezing.

10. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough has a density of about 0.2 to about 0.5 g/cm³.

11. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the gas bubbles comprise gas produced by the spent yeast component during proofing, and wherein the preserved yeast component is physically separated from or protected from the gas-producing activity of the spent yeast component during the proofing stage.

12. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the frozen dough is in its final shape and form for baking.

13. (Currently Amended) A method for making a frozen dough product, the method comprising: (a) mixing dough ingredients to produce a dough composition, the dough ingredients comprising: i. water; ii. flour; iii. a first yeast that is unencapsulated or unprotected; and iv. a second yeast that is encapsulated, fat-coated, or otherwise protected; (b) proofing the dough at a temperature and for a duration sufficient to substantially deplete the fermentative activity of the first yeast while preserving the viability of the second yeast, wherein during proofing the first yeast produces gas and is spent and the second yeast remains viable and is preserved; and (c) freezing the dough after proofing.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein at least 60% of the first yeast is spent during proofing, such that the first yeast has less than 40% of its initial vitality after the proofing step.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein at least 50% of the second yeast is preserved during proofing, such that the second yeast retains at least 50% of its initial vitality after the proofing step.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 1 to about 7 wt.% of the first yeast.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the second yeast.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the second yeast is different from the first yeast in that the second yeast is encapsulated, fat-coated, or otherwise protected, whereas the first yeast is unencapsulated and unprotected.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the second yeast comprises encapsulated yeast, fat-coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof, wherein the encapsulation or coating provides protection to the yeast during freezing and frozen storage.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the mixing comprises mixing the water, flour, and first yeast for a first period of time, adding the second yeast and mixing the dough ingredients for a second period of time, wherein the first period of time is longer than the second period of time, such that the first yeast undergoes substantial fermentation before the second yeast is introduced.

21. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 20, wherein the second period of time is from about 1 to about 2 minutes, such that the second yeast is minimally fermented during the mixing stage.

22. (Original) The method of claim 13, further comprising: shaping and cutting the dough to produce a pizza crust prior to proofing; freezing the pizza crust; and applying toppings to the frozen pizza crust.

23. (Original) The method of claim 13, further comprising refrigerating the dough after freezing.

24. (Original) The method of claim 23, wherein the dough is refrigerated for from about 12 hours to about 7 days.

25. (Currently Amended) A method for making a leavened bakery product, the method comprising: (a) mixing dough ingredients to produce a dough, the dough ingredients comprising: i. water; ii. flour; iii. a first yeast that is unencapsulated or unprotected; and iv. a second yeast that is encapsulated, fat-coated, or otherwise protected; (b) proofing the dough to produce a proofed dough at a temperature and for a duration sufficient to substantially deplete the fermentative activity of the first yeast while preserving the viability of the second yeast, wherein the first yeast is spent during the proofing and produces gas, and the second yeast is preserved during the proofing and remains viable; (c) freezing the proofed dough; and (d) baking the dough to produce the leavened bakery product, wherein the second yeast produces additional gas during the baking step.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the second yeast is different from the first yeast in that the second yeast is encapsulated, fat-coated, or otherwise protected, whereas the first yeast is unencapsulated and unprotected.

27. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the second yeast comprises encapsulated yeast, fat-coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof, wherein the encapsulation or coating protects the yeast during freezing and frozen storage.

28. (Original) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough does not comprise chemical leaveners.

29. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough has a first volume before the proofing step, a second volume after the proofing step, and a third volume after the baking step, and wherein the third volume is at least 50% greater than the second volume, wherein the increase in volume during baking is at least in part due to gas production by the second yeast.

30. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 29, wherein the third volume is greater than the second volume due at least in part to an activity of the second yeast during the baking step, wherein the second yeast produces gas that was not produced during the proofing stage.

31. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 20 to about 40 wt.% water and about 50 to about 70 wt.% flour.

32. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 1 to about 7 wt.% of the first yeast.

33. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the second yeast.
